guard.title: Protection
guard.enable: Stop the account automatically (emergency stop) when a loss limit is used up to
guard.usage: Share of the daily or max loss limit (%)
guard.hint: For bots without a reliable daily stop of their own. wickwatch checks every ACCOUNT_POLL_SECONDS (default 60 s) and acts once per trading day: it stops the account's instances, cancels all orders and closes all positions, manual ones too. Instances stay stopped until you start them. A second line of defence – it does not replace a stop inside the bot.
guard.needsLimit: Needs a daily or max loss limit.

instance.managedLabels: Set by wickwatch from the configuration.

confirm.emergencyStop: Stop all instances on account {account}, cancel pending orders and close all positions?

templates.changesHint: Untick a value to keep the current one, e.g. a licence key that belongs to this account.

templates.kept: Not in the template, the current value stays: {names}
templates.applyHint: Saved as a new version. The bot keeps running with its configuration until you apply the version.
templates.applied: Version {version} saved from the template. Apply it to use it in the bot.

apiTokens.deleteConfirm: Delete the token {name}? Scripts and clients using it lose access.
apiTokens.name: Name
apiTokens.nameHint: What uses it, e.g. the AI client or script.
apiTokens.roleHint: Viewer is enough for MCP clients and monitoring: they only read.
apiTokens.confirmHint: A token gives lasting access, so creating one asks for your password again (and the code, with 2FA on).
apiTokens.needs2fa: Creating tokens needs 2FA on this server (API_TOKENS_REQUIRE_2FA).
apiTokens.copyNow: Copy the token now. It is not shown again; only its first characters stay in the list.
apiTokens.mcpIntro: AI clients that speak the Model Context Protocol read accounts, instances, logs and alerts here. It is read-only; log text written by bots reaches the model as untrusted data.
apiTokens.mcpOffHint: Switched off on the server (MCP=off). API tokens still work for the REST API.
